objectives.wording: Map ear, nose, throat and head and neck structures to their functions.
Explain the mechanism of chronic otitis media.
Present the history and findings and justify investigations and management.
Recognize extracranial and intracranial warning signs and justify urgent evaluation.
Explain the mechanism of otosclerosis.
Relate clinical and audiometric findings to workup and management options.
Explain the mechanisms of adenotonsillitis.
Elicit, document and present a focused ENT history in simulation.
Demonstrate headlamp, nasal speculum and tongue depressor use and examine the ear, sinuses and neck, including assessment of laryngeal crepitus.
Demonstrate otoscopy and perform and interpret tuning fork tests.
Explain test technique and interpret sample pure-tone and impedance audiograms.
Demonstrate otoscope handling, assess membrane mobility and sketch and interpret the findings.
Select and interpret representative imaging, microbiology and histology results.
Identify instruments for representative ear, nasal and throat operations, foreign body removal and tracheostomy and explain their uses.
Elicit risk factors and identify suspicious premalignant and malignant findings on a simulated examination.
Role-play informed consent for representative ear, nose and throat procedures.
Simulate resuscitation, anterior nasal packing, airway escalation including tracheostomy and appropriate foreign body management.
Demonstrate correct instillation of topical ear, nose and throat medicines in simulation.
Compare national hearing and cancer prevention activities and noise and pollution controls, and participate in a hearing awareness activity.
Observe otomicroscopy and describe indications, setup and examination steps.
Observe diagnostic endoscopy and explain indications, preparation and landmarks.
Compare observed rigid and flexible examinations by indications and steps.
Present a focused history and distinguish primary from referred pain using findings, tests and management priorities.
Present a focused history, recognize representative external ear disorders and justify investigations and care.
Use a simulated history and otoscopic findings to justify investigations and management.
Present the history and use otoscopy and hearing findings to justify assessment and follow-up.
Present a focused history, localize the source and justify examination, testing and management.
Recognize possible cholesteatoma in a simulated case and justify assessment and referral.
Demonstrate removal on a simulator and explain when the chosen technique is unsuitable.
Explain the indications and steps of myringotomy.
Explain the indications and steps of tympanoplasty.
Observe a demonstration and explain indications, landmarks and major steps.
Recognize representative findings and justify investigations and management options.
Differentiate conductive and sensorineural patterns and explain assessment of sudden and noise-induced loss.
Recognize age-specific signs and outline testing, intervention and follow-up.
Relate tube anatomy to dysfunction and compare findings, tests and management.
Localize weakness and justify investigations and care, including eye protection.
Differentiate peripheral and central patterns and explain vestibular testing and management priorities.
Recognize the characteristic symptom pattern and explain assessment and management.
Classify tinnitus by features and explain investigations and management by presentation.
Present a focused history and distinguish unilateral and bilateral causes using examination and appropriate tests.
Explain assessment and management and describe indications and observed steps of septoplasty.
Present a focused history and explain findings, investigation and management.
Elicit exposure and symptom patterns and justify assessment and management.
Use a simulated history to distinguish nonallergic triggers and justify management.
Compare presentation and causes and justify investigation and management in representative cases.
Present a focused history and distinguish typical polyposis from findings requiring further workup.
Demonstrate initial assessment, localize likely bleeding and justify investigations and management.
Recognize clinical features in a sample case and justify diagnostic testing and management options.
Identify airway and other urgent risks and explain investigations and stabilization priorities.
Recognize the characteristic presentation and explain safe evaluation and referral.
Present a focused history, compare acute and chronic findings and justify investigations, management and escalation for complications.
Compare warning signs and select imaging, diagnostic and referral pathways.
Compare representative causes and justify targeted investigations and management.
Distinguish obstructive, inflammatory and neoplastic presentations and justify workup and management.
Recognize warning signs and explain airway assessment, imaging and escalation priorities.
Present a focused history, distinguish oropharyngeal and oesophageal patterns and justify testing and management.
Present a focused history, compare acute and chronic findings and identify complications and management priorities.
Explain the indications, major steps and complications of tonsillectomy.
Explain the indications, major steps and complications of adenoidectomy.
Present a focused history and justify examination, investigations and referral based on duration and warning signs.
Compare benign lesions, acute and chronic inflammation and paralysis by presentation, workup and management.
Recognise presentations of laryngeal cancer and explain diagnostic evaluation and management.
Recognise presentations of hypopharyngeal cancer and explain diagnostic evaluation and management.
Use timing and associated signs to localize obstruction and prioritize airway assessment.
Observe a demonstration and explain indications, major steps and postoperative tube care.
Compare representative presentations and justify investigations and management principles.
Recognise representative ear, nose and throat manifestations of HIV infection and explain investigation and care.
Trace light through the eye and neural signals to visual cortex and explain image formation.
Classify refractive errors and use ray diagrams to explain correction.
Demonstrate distance, near, colour and pinhole testing and assessment of menace and blink responses.
Compare indications and optical principles of representative procedures.
Classify amblyopia and explain early detection, prevention and treatment of refractive amblyopia.
Compare styes, lid malposition, lagophthalmos, blepharitis and preseptal cellulitis by cause, findings and care.
Under supervision demonstrate Bell phenomenon assessment and ptosis evaluation.
Under supervision demonstrate lacrimal assessment, including regurgitation and syringing tests.
Recognize typical findings and sight-threatening complications and explain management priorities.
Distinguish orbital from preseptal infection and explain urgent evaluation and management.
Recognize ocular and neurological clues and justify urgent escalation in simulation.
Use onset, direction and associated findings to narrow causes and plan assessment.
Classify representative orbital tumours and compare their presentations.
Select investigations and identify management and referral priorities.
Elicit a focused history and distinguish likely causes and red flags.
Compare bacterial and viral mechanisms, findings and management.
Compare causes and explain trachoma progression, complications and control.
Compare allergic presentations and explain vernal disease complications and management.
Explain risk factors, clinical differentiation and management.
Demonstrate removal of a superficial foreign body on a simulator and recognize when removal is unsafe.
Identify a superficial corneal foreign body and demonstrate safe removal on a simulator.
Demonstrate instillation and counsel a simulated patient using teach-back.
Relate corneal layers, hydration and surface integrity to transparency.
Classify representative congenital and inflammatory corneal disorders.
Compare likely agents using risk factors and lesion findings and justify investigation and urgent referral.
Grade supplied corneal opacities and compare management options.
Relate tear film dysfunction to causes, findings and management.
Use an applicable definition of blindness and classify the major corneal causes.
Compare causes of visual impairment and explain the Indian blindness programme and Vision 2020 using official material.
Compare transplant types by tissue layer and indication.
Explain donation and demonstrate the simulated documentation and coordination workflow.
Role-play counselling relatives and explain preservation pending retrieval using the eye bank protocol.
Compare clinical forms and explain assessment, complications and care.
Compare systemic associations of episcleritis and scleritis and identify referral indications.
Classify uveitis by site and distinguish granulomatous and nongranulomatous anterior findings.
Connect complications and likely causes to investigation and treatment principles.
Explain systemic associations and demonstrate counselling on follow-up and warning symptoms.
Recognise hyphema and compare its causes.
Recognise hypopyon and compare its causes.
Recognize typical presentation and explain pathogenesis and management.
Relate mechanism and optic nerve findings to assessment and treatment.
Explain treatment options, adverse effects, prognosis and follow-up of glaucoma in simulated counselling.
Recognize a simulated acute presentation and prioritize initial assessment and urgent care.
Classify secondary mechanisms using representative causes.
Identify capsule, zonules and lens structures and relate them to operative steps.
Classify causes, stages and complications using representative cases.
Demonstrate assessment and counsel a simulated patient about surgery.
Demonstrate an assigned supervised or simulated team role and explain safety checks.
Compare surgical and anaesthetic approaches and outline ECCE steps, complications and postoperative care.
Elicit history and signs in simulation and compare optical rehabilitation options.
Demonstrate direct and indirect techniques and identify normal fundus landmarks.
Grade representative findings and explain mechanisms, screening and management principles.
Compare arterial and venous presentations and explain urgent assessment and care pathways.

Compare characteristic findings and management priorities for hypertensive retinopathy, ROP, Eales disease, detachment, central serous disease, cystoid oedema, AMD, retinitis pigmentosa and retinoblastoma.
Localize sample defects and select diagnostic tests, imaging and management pathways.
Demonstrate examination of monocular and binocular movements and document findings.
Classify heterotropias, interpret representative alignment tests and identify referral indications.
Explain when refractive correction may help and identify signs requiring referral.
Classify ocular manifestations, explain causes and outline management and referral.
Compare indications for enucleation, evisceration and exenteration.
Classify injuries and explain initial care and referral priorities in simulated cases.
